answer: A harmless piece of a germ.
B cells, but only the few whose shape fits the piece; they multiply and make antibodies.
Memory cells: some of the responding B cells stay behind as memory cells.
When the real germ shows up, the matching memory cells are already waiting, so they strike in days, not weeks.
About 3 matching (orange) B cells out of roughly 36 dots shown (4 rows of 9), one matching cell in each of the top three rows. I counted the dots by eye; the clip gave no number.
